exposure: Ureaplasma parvum (U. parvum) in amniotic fluids
outcome: early spontaneous preterm labor (<32 gestational weeks)
preterm premature rupture of the membranes (PPROM)
cohort: The study included 2419 singleton pregnant women who underwent genetic amniocentesis for fetal CNV-seq testing and had documented pregnancy outcomes.
finding: High abundance of asymptomatic Ureaplasma parvum in amniotic fluids is statistically associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, specifically early spontaneous preterm labor (<32 gestational weeks) and preterm premature rupture of the membranes.
